name: Chronic Intestinal Pseudoobstruction Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Chronic Intestinal Pseudoobstruction

criteria.description: Chronic or recurrent symptoms of intestinal obstruction without mechanical cause
Radiologic evidence of dilated bowel loops and air-fluid levels consistent with obstruction
Abnormal intestinal manometry demonstrating impaired motility
Exclusion of mechanical obstruction by endoscopy or imaging
Histopathologic evidence of visceral neuropathy or myopathy in intestinal biopsies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic symptoms of obstruction without mechanical cause, radiologic evidence of obstruction, abnormal manometry, and exclusion of mechanical obstruction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including imaging, motility studies, and exclusion of mechanical causes.

imaging: Abdominal X-ray showing dilated bowel loops with air-fluid levels
genetic: Mutations in genes related to enteric nervous system or smooth muscle (e.g., ACTG2, MYH11) in familial cases
other: Abnormal intestinal manometry demonstrating impaired peristalsis
Histopathology showing visceral neuropathy or myopathy

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of mechanical cause on imaging or endoscopy
Congenital absence of enteric ganglion cells
Usually presents in neonates or infants
Associated systemic autoimmune or metabolic disease
Improvement with treatment of underlying disease

redFlags: Signs of bowel ischemia or perforation
references: Knowles CH, De Giorgio R, Kapur RP, et al. Chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction: clinical and molecular insights. Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2013;10(7):386-397.
American Gastroenterological Association medical position statement on chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction. Gastroenterology. 2007;132(5):1909-1914.
